note: U1 is a library and provisions no infrastructure, so the per-kind applicability produces cicd-pipeline.md and this file only. Every NFR9.x from NFR Design is enumerated. Those with a distinct pipeline element are OK against the step that runs them; those enforced wholly inside the module are N/A with the step that exercises them named, rather than omitted. Two were GAP through this stage and are now CLOSED: NFR9.30 could not execute in B1 (no table, no endpoint) and NFR9.32 was the cross-Bolt DoD amendment that would give it an owner. They were deliberately left GAP rather than marked N/A, because marking them N/A would have made the sensor pass while asserting something false - they were not inapplicable to this Unit, they were unowned - and amending another Bolt's definition of done was a delivery-planning decision outside this stage's scope. The human took that decision at Code Generation on 2026-10-18: bolt-plan.md B2's DoD now carries the OpenAPI money-pattern assertion and B3's the column type-and-precision assertion, so both rows are now OK. Separately, NFR9.7 and NFR9.9 were corrected from N/A to OK at review: both had been deferred to B4's Android job, which concealed a real gap behind rows that read as settled, when U1's own catalogue entry and B1's DoD both require the Kotlin money type and its loud-failure serializer to ship in this Bolt. Step 11 now covers them. One further correction at iteration 2: a per-push no-credential invariant had been written as 'NFR9.33' and added to upstream_ids, inventing a requirement no upstream artifact contains. It is a stage-originated decision and now sits in the reverse array with the others.

reverse.target: cicd-pipeline A - every step in the per-push blocking suite must run on a fresh clone with no credential; a step needing one belongs in the release gate. A stage-originated decision, NOT an upstream requirement: it was briefly written as 'NFR9.33' and placed in upstream_ids, which invented a requirement no upstream artifact contains - the NFR9 series ends at NFR9.32. Recorded here because the reverse array is where this file already carries stage-originated decisions. The invariant is about credentials rather than toolchains: step 11's Android SDK and B3's Docker daemon are prerequisites, not secrets; B4's DEX scan needs a signing keystore and is therefore the first and only scheduled exception

A scoping decision with no single upstream requirement: team.md sequences the whole toolchain at skeleton time and B1 is skeleton time, so this document specifies the project's backend pipeline with B1's steps filled in. Scoping it to U1 alone would describe something that does not exist and leave B2 reinventing the foundation

From team.md Testing Posture rather than a numbered NFR: one make check target identical locally and in CI, because a gate reproducible only by pushing gets bypassed. The corollary that the blocking suite needs no secret is absolute for B1 and is a property later Bolts must defend

From team.md Way of Working: with squash-merge and one reviewer, the post-merge run is the only thing that catches a PR green against an older main. Branch protection requires the CI check but no approvals, since a required approval from the sole author is theatre

A pipeline decision: cache dependencies keyed on the lockfile hash, nothing else. Test-result and incremental-lint caching save seconds at this scale and introduce a stale cache masking a real failure, which is the defect class this Unit's control set exists to prevent

From team.md Deployment: images tagged with the commit SHA and latest never deployed. B1 builds no image, but the convention is set here because it is a supply-chain control making a deployed artifact identifiable, and retrofitting it after images exist is harder than declaring it now

cicd-pipeline G - a library has no compute, network, storage, environment, database, cache, queue, CDN, DNS or load balancer, and no runtime signal to monitor: its correctness is established before release rather than observed at runtime. The absences are enumerated individually so a reader finds the reason rather than an absence to interpret

cicd-pipeline A - B4's DEX scan is pinned to the R8-minified release build, which needs a signing keystore. team.md names only three secrets (gateway credentials, JWT signing key, database URL). Settled here rather than discovered at B4: it is a fourth named secret with the same rotation-runbook treatment, and the scan sits in the release gate rather than the per-push suite

cicd-pipeline E - replaces an unmechanised 'checked rather than assumed' obligation with 60% review and 80% migrate-to-CodeBuild thresholds against the 2,000 min free tier, checked monthly. A hard stop at 2,000 means no CI at all until the month rolls over, on a project where CI is the only gate

cicd-pipeline B step 2 and E - step 11 introduces a Gradle build, so lockfile and checksum verification must cover both surfaces. team.md names dependencyVerification as the only control detecting a tampered or substituted Gradle artifact; verifying only the Python lockfile would leave the Kotlin surface, which carries the client half of the money boundary from B1 onward, with no supply-chain control at all
